Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 31 s. 2023 MAY 04 2023 DIR. MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN Regional Director, DILG-NCR Annex Building, Sugar Center Compound North Avenue, Dlliman, Quezon City Dear RD Agustin: This has reference to your letter dated January 12, 2023 regarding the query raised by the Alabang Senior Citizens' Association on whether barangay personnel (elective or appointive) can participate in elections for Barangay Senior Citizens Association (BSCAs). The following points of clarification were raised as to the type of treatment to the following BSCAs in relation to the qualification of a barangay personnel to run for a position, to wit: (1) Government or LGU-funded BSCAs, including those whose officers receive honorarium or allowances from the government or LGUs; and (2) BSCAs operating through private contributions of members. Our NBOO gave its initial position on the matter, to wit: (1) The establishment of a Senior Citizens Organization/Association is mandated at the city and municipal levels and funds for the operation of OSCA shall be included in the annual appropriation of the City and Municipal government; (2) As the law does not provide for the establishment of an Office for Senior Citizen Affairs (OSCA) at the barangay level, thus, the BSCAs may be considered as a barangay-based non-government organization (BB-NGO) organized by the Senior Citizens in a particular barangay. And [sic] the funds for its effective operations may come from the contributions of its members. (3) Barangay officials who are senior citizens may not be prohibited from joining BSCA, either as officers or members, as long as their participation in BSCA does not tend to be-in conflict with their officials' functions as barangay officials. (4) Likewise, barangay officials who are Senior Citizens may be allowed to participate in any election of the Senior Citizen's organization/association, where they are members. However, a Senior Citizen-Barangay Official shall not be appointed by the City or Municipal Mayor as the head of the City/Municipal Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

OSCA as the same is prohibited under Sec. 951 of RA 7160 and other existing Civil Service Rules and Regulation. Consistent with the NBOO findings and Rule VI, Art. 21 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 9994, the OSCA shall be established in cities and municipalities only. The matter before us concerns a BSCA, which is neither established in a city or a municipality, but at a barangay level. Hence, we agree with the findings of the NBOO, that the BSCA, performing similar functions as the OSCA, is not a government sanctioned entity and funding may be highly dependent on private contributions and fund raising activities of its own. Accordingly, the prohibition on Section 95 of the LGC is not applicable herein. On the discussion of conflict of interest, we refer the matter to DILG Legal Opinion No. 49. s. 20072 which discussed the pertinent laws related to the matter: Section 3(i) of RA 6713, as amended otherwise known as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees defines conflict of interest in the following manner: (i) "Conflict of interest" arises when a public official or employee is a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business, and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty. In relation thereto, Sec. 7 and 9 of the same Code providing for the legal consequences when conflict of interest arises, provides and we quote: Sec. 7. Prohibited Acts and Transactions - In addition to acts and omissions of public officials and employees now prescribed in the Constitution and existing laws, the following shall constitute prohibited acts and transactions of any public official and employee and are hereby declared to be unlawful: (a) Financial and material interest - public officials and employees shall not directly or indirectly have any financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their Office. (b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto - public officials and employees during their incumbency, shall not: (i) own, control, manage or accept employment as officer, employee, consultant, broker, agent, trustee or nominee in any private enterprise regulated, supervised or licensed by their office unless expressly allowed by law xxx xxx Sec. 9. A public official or employee shall avoid conflict of interest at all times. When a conflict of interest arises, he shall resign from his position in a ny private business enterprise within thirty (30) days from his assumption of office and/or divest himself of his shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from such assumption. xxx xxx xxx 1 Sec. 95. Additional or Double Compensation. - No elective or appointive local official or employee shall receive additional, double, or indirect compensation, unless specifically authorized by law, nor accept without the consent of Congress, any present, emoluments, Office, or title Of any kind from any foreign government. Pensions or gratuities shall not be considered as additional. double, or indirect compensation. 2 July 8, 2007. Page 2 of 3

Based on the foregoing, conflict of interest arises whenever a public official or employee but faithfully performing his official duty, may oppose or affect the interest of a private corporation or business to which he is also affiliated, either as a member of a board, officer or a substantial stockholder. Accordingly, if the faithful performance of his official duty will not oppose or affect the interest of a private corporation or business to which he is affiliated, there is no conflict of interest to speak of. Thus, we can aptly say that conflict of interest does not ipso facto arise whenever a public official or employee holds another position in a private corporation or business. To our mind, the rationale behind the prohibition on conflict of interest and the consequent mandatory divestment under Sec. 9 of RA 6713 is that no public officer shall be permitted to entertain two (2) conflicting loyalties one, public, and other, private, with regard to matters brought before his consideration. Experience consistently tells us that where private interest clashes with the duty to uphold public interest, the tendency is that the concerned public officer will favor his personal interest. The test of conflict of interest is therefore whether the activity, investment, relationship or interest involving the private corporation or business to which a public official or employee is affiliated may prevent him from faithfully discharging his duty as such public official or employee. Otherwise, there arises no conflict of interest. (e.g. performance of a ministerial duty) In the afore quoted provisions, in sum, a public official or employee's faithful performance of his official duty may oppose or affect the interest of a private corporation or business to which he is also affiliated when said public official or employee (1) directly or indirectly, have any financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of his office; (2) directly or indirectly having financial or pecuniary interest in any business, contract or transaction in connection with which he intervenes or takes part in his official capacity, or in which he is prohibited by the Constitution or any law from having any interest, and (3) own, control, manage or accept employment as officer, employee, consultant, counsel, broker, agent, trustee or nominee in any private enterprise regulated, supervised or licensed by their office unless expressly allowed by law. Applying the foregoing to the instant case, this level opines that barangay official/personnel can participate in elections for the BSCAs. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . JUA VICTOR R. LLAMAS ersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs LLLS/RPB/LRALLD/sbVclp Page 3 of 3
